ja: פהו אלשקי אלד'י יכ'אב סעיה פי אלדניא ויחבט אג'רה פי אלאכ'רה. ואלעאקל יג'רי פי אלוג'וה אלת'לאת'ה עלי מא יואפק דינה ודניאה, ות'קתה במא פי יד אללה מן רזקה וכסבה אקוי מן ת'קתה במא פי ידה מן ד'לך, אן לא יעלם אן כאן הו רזק גד'א או רזק מלך, פינאל אלכראמה פי אלדניא וחסן אלמאאל פי אלאכ'רה, כמא קאל פי מזמור הללויה אשרי איש ירא את ה' אלי אכ'רה. ומן אלנאס טבקאת לא יג'תהדון פי כסב אלמאל ואלאכת'אר מנה אלא חבא פי אלכראמה מן אלנאס ונשר אלד'כר פיהם, פלא יקנעהם מנה שי, וד'לך ג'הלא מנהם באסבאב אלכראמה פי אלדניא ואלאכ'רה, ויחמלהם עלי ד'לך מא ישאהדון מן תבג'יל אלעאמה לד'וי אלאמואל וכראמתהם להם טמעא פימא ענדהם וחרצא לאסתג'לאב מא פי אידיהם, ולו עקלוא ותיקנוא אן ליס פי קותהם ולא פי טאקתהם דפע פלס מנהא אלא למן קדרה אללה לה ענדהם, למא אמלוא גיר אללה ג'ל ועז, ולא אסתוג'ב אלכראמה ענדהם אלא מן כ'צה אללה בפצ'איל מחמודה יסתחק להא כראמהֵ אללה תעאלי, כקולה כי מכבדי אכבד ובוזי יקלו. פלמא ג'הלת אלעאמה פי אכראמהם לד'וי אלאמואל אסבאב אלכראמה, זאדהם ד'לך ג'הלא באסבאב מטלובהם, פוקעוא פי חרץ חת'ית' וג'הד וכיד טול אעמארהם, ואגפלוא מא כאן אוג'ב עליהם אלג'אתהאד פיה ואלחרץ מן תופיהֵ חקוק אללה תעאלי קבלהם, ושכר נעמה לדיהם, וכאן מטלובהם אקרב אליהם בהד'א אלסביל לא מחאלה, כקולה אורך ימים בימינה בשמאלה עשר וכבוד,

**The second aspect**: that he reckons all that comes to him of wealth to be the sustenance of his nourishment, not realizing that sustenance is divided into three divisions. The first: the sustenance of his nourishment — the subsistence of his body alone — which is the guaranteed-from-God for every living being to the conclusion of his term. The second: the sustenance of the nourishment of others under him — dependents, children, attendants, retinue, and the like — which is not guaranteed by God (exalted be He) for all servants but for the elect of them, with specific conditions; this is an accident, made ready at one time and not another, according to what the currents of judgments from God in bounty and justice oblige. The third: the sustenance of property — namely, the wealth from which the human has no benefit, and upon him is its keeping and protecting, until he bequeaths it to another or it perishes from him. The ignorant reckons all that has been decreed for him of wealth to be the sustenance of his nourishment and the subsistence of his body, so he gulps after it and is eager for it; perhaps he gathers it for the husband of his wife after him, and his killer, and the bitterest enemy he has.

**The third aspect**: that he delivers the sustenances to their owners — what God has decreed for them through his hand — and reproaches them for it; he wishes to attract their thanks, to multiply their praise for it, and the rendering-of-service to him on its account. His soul grows haughty, conceit and self-glory enter him, and he turns away from thanks to God (exalted be He) for it. He has supposed that, were he to have withheld it from them, it would have remained with him; and that, were it not for him, their sustenances would have been cut off. He is the wretched one whose striving is disappointed in this world and whose reward is destroyed in the next. The intelligent runs in the three aspects according to what agrees with his religion and his this-world, his confidence in what is in the hand of God concerning his sustenance and his earning being stronger than his confidence in what is in his own hand of that — for he does not know whether it is sustenance of nourishment or sustenance of property; so he attains honor in this world and a beautiful end in the next, as it says in the psalm "Hallelujah, happy is the man who fears the Lord" to the end (Psalms 112).

There are ranks among people who do not labor in the earning of wealth and the multiplying of it except out of love of honor from people and the spreading of fame among them; nothing of it satisfies them — and that is from their ignorance of the causes of honor in this world and the next. What carries them to this is what they observe of the populace exalting the possessors of wealth and honoring them out of greed for what is with them and eagerness for the attracting of what is in their hands. If they were intelligent and certain that it is not in their power nor their capacity to deliver a single coin of it except to the one for whom God has decreed it with them — they would not hope in any but God (mighty and exalted), nor reckon as deserving honor with them any but the one whom God has singled out with praiseworthy excellences who is worthy of God's honor (exalted be He), as He said: "For those who honor Me I shall honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed" (1 Samuel 2:30). When the populace, in their honoring of the possessors of wealth, is ignorant of the causes of honor, this increases them in ignorance of the causes of what they seek; they fall into intense eagerness, exertion, and stratagem throughout their lives — heedless of what was more incumbent upon them of striving and eagerness in fulfilling the dues of God (exalted be He) toward Him and thanksgiving for His blessing toward them; and what they sought would have been closer to them by this path without fail, as He said: "Length of days is in her right hand; in her left, riches and honor" (Proverbs 3:16); and He said: "And wealth and honor come from before You, and You rule over all; and in Your hand are power and might; and in Your hand it is to make great and to strengthen all" (1 Chronicles 29:12).
